# CrimeLens Kerala — complete CNN/LSTM demo project

This repository contains a Streamlit dashboard, official historical data extracts, a reproducible synthetic-data generator/training pipeline, and saved CNN/LSTM weights. It includes all 14 Kerala districts and example area options including Pazhayannur, Chelakkara, and Lakkidi.

## Critical data and accuracy note

**The included CNN and LSTM weights are trained on synthetic demonstration data only.** The 60,000-row `data/synthetic_demo_events.csv` and `data/synthetic_demo_monthly_series.csv` were generated by code from assumptions for testing the end-to-end pipeline. They are not real crime reports. The CNN's holdout accuracy and LSTM's MAE in `models/training_metrics.json` measure agreement with synthetic labels only and must not be advertised as real-world crime prediction accuracy. Synthetic augmentation does not create real evidence or improve real-world accuracy.

The official CSVs are kept separate:
- `data/kerala_police_statewide_ipc_bns_2020_2026.csv`: statewide annual crime-head counts from Kerala Police; 2026 figures are partial-year where indicated.
- `data/pazhayannur_police_station_stats.csv`: historical figures transcribed from the Pazhayannur Police Station official statistics page.
- `data/kerala_14_districts_coverage.csv`: area options for app navigation only, not crime records.

Official sources:
- Kerala Police IPC/BNS statistics: https://keralapolice.gov.in/crime-statistics/ipc-cases
- Kerala Police total cases: https://keralapolice.gov.in/crime/total-cases
- Pazhayannur Police Station crime statistics: https://ps.keralapolice.gov.in/pazhayannur-ps/crime-statistics
- Kerala OGD / NCRB Crime in India 2021: https://kerala.data.gov.in/catalog/crime-india-2021

## Run locally

Python 3.11 or 3.12 recommended.

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
streamlit run app.py
```

The saved weights are in `models/` and load automatically. The app does not need an API key.

## Retrain the demonstration models

```bash
python training/train_models.py
```

This recreates the synthetic CSVs, `models/cnn_demo_weights.pt`, `models/lstm_demo_weights.pt`, scaler JSON files, and synthetic-only metrics. Do not mix synthetic rows into an official dataset without keeping a clear provenance label.

## Deploy on Streamlit Community Cloud

1. Extract this ZIP.
2. Upload the contents of the `CrimeLens_Kerala_Advanced` folder to a GitHub repository (not the parent folder as an extra nesting level).
3. In Streamlit Community Cloud, choose **Create app**, select the repository and `app.py`, and deploy.
4. Keep `requirements.txt`, `.python-version`, `models/`, and `data/` in the repository. Model files are small enough for this demo.

Render users can use the included `render.yaml`, though free-tier limits and package build times may change.

## How to get a defensible real-world model

Collect a sufficiently large event-level dataset from authorized police/open-government sources with dates, station or geocoded location, crime type, and consistent reporting periods. Keep an untouched time-based test set. Compare simple baselines (seasonal naive, Poisson/negative-binomial regression, gradient boosting) before CNN/LSTM. Evaluate with MAE/RMSE for counts and precision/recall/calibration for classifications. Do not infer town-level risk by distributing statewide totals across towns. Crime statistics reflect reporting and enforcement as well as underlying incidents; never use this app to determine that an individual place is safe or unsafe.
